![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `torchaudio.functional.forced_align` function requires that the target sequence does not contain any blank tokens. It's crucial to add an assertion to validate this precondition. Without this check, the function might fail with an unclear error message from within `torchaudio` or produce incorrect alignments if the input `ys_pad` contains blank tokens.

```suggestion
        assert not (ys_pad == blank_idx).any(), "Target cannot contain blank tokens."
        align_label, align_prob = torchaudio.functional.forced_align(
            log_probs, ys_pad, hlens, ys_lens, blank=blank_idx
        )
```

         return torch.argmax(self.ctc_lo(hs_pad), dim=2)
+    
+    def forced_align(self, hs_pad, hlens, ys_pad, ys_lens, blank_idx=0):
+        """Force alignment between input and target sequences (Viterbi path).
+        Args:
+            hs_pad: batch of padded hidden state sequences (B, Tmax, D)
+            hlens: batch of lengths of hidden state sequences (B)
+            ys_pad: batch of padded character id sequence tensor (B, Lmax)
+            ys_lens: batch of lengths of character sequence (B)
+            blank_idx: index of blank symbol
+            Note: B must be 1.
+        Returns:
+            alignments: Tuple(tensor, tensor):
+                - Label for each time step in the alignment path computed using forced alignment.
+                - Log probability scores of the labels for each time step.
+            https://docs.pytorch.org/audio/main/generated/torchaudio.functional.forced_align.html
+        """
+        import torchaudio
+        if self.ctc_type != "builtin":
+            raise NotImplementedError("force_align is only implemented for builtin CTC")
+        log_probs = self.log_softmax(hs_pad)  # (B, Tmax, odim)
+        assert log_probs.size(0) == 1, "Forced alignment only works with batch size 1."
+        align_label, align_prob = torchaudio.functional.forced_align(
+            log_probs, ys_pad, hlens, ys_lens, blank=blank_idx
+        )

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Modifying the input tensor `text` in-place is a side effect that can lead to unexpected behavior and hard-to-debug issues in the calling code. It's much safer to create a new tensor with the modifications, for example by using `torch.where` or by cloning the tensor before modification.

```suggestion
        text = torch.where(text == -1, self.ignore_id, text)
```
